subject: QuantumEdge long-term commercial posture & uplift guard — executive authorization request
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Park <lena.park@quantumedge.com>, procurement@quantumedge.com
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Commercial summary and next steps (QED-2026-042)

Hi Lena / QuantumEdge procurement team —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Per our conversation, attached is a concise term summary that reflects the commercial we discussed: a two-year commitment, reserved capacity for your sustained throughput, and a price lock for the first 24 months. Key items to highlight:

- 24-month price lock at listed unit rates (see Term_Summary)
- Annual uplift guard at 5% (cap on list price increases during the committed period)
- Renewal protection: guarantee of no one-off renewal uplift >10% in the first renewal window, subject to usage thresholds

We also attached a preliminary SOW for the initial onboarding and a draft term sheet. Please review and flag any legal or procurement questions.

Next steps: if the commercial posture is acceptable, we can circulate a clean term sheet and route for procurement review + DocuSign. Grace from Deal Desk is cc'd and will handle any nonstandard term coordination.

Attachments: QuantumEdge_Term_Summary_v5.pdf, QED_SOW_v2.docx

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0197

From: Lena Park <lena.park@quantumedge.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@quantumedge.com
Date: Thu, 03 Dec 2026 11:34:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Commercial summary and next steps (QED-2026-042)

Aditya —

Appreciate the summary. A few procurement points we need clarified before legal will sign off:

1) The 5% uplift cap during the commitment period: can you confirm whether that is applied to list or to our committed unit rate? We need it guaranteed against any list-rate repricing.
2) Renewal protections look fine in principle, but procurement wants a floor/ceiling mechanism: if market prices rise sharply, we need a defined cap on renewal increases and an option for a one-time extension at the original uplift guard.
3) SLA credits: we will require a 99.5% uptime target with defined credits for breaches.

Can you route these to your deal desk so we can close the few gaps? We aim to finish vendor selection by 12/20.

—Lena
Head of Cloud Ops, QuantumEdge
lena.park@quantumedge.com

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 04 Dec 2026 08:07:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Commercial summary and next steps (QED-2026-042) — deal desk posture suggestion

Grace / Aditya —

Reviewed procurement notes from QuantumEdge. Proposed deal desk posture for exec authorization:

- Keep the 24-month price lock tied to the committed unit rate (not list). This protects QED from surprise list increases while preserving our headroom.
- Maintain a 5% annual uplift cap on list adjustments during the commitment. For clarity, the customer gets the lower of (committed unit rate) or (list rate - uplift cap).
- Add explicit renewal protection: at first renewal window, any increase >10% triggers a mandatory commercial review and gives QED the option to renew at prior year rates for a one-time 12-month bridge.
- SLA: we can accept 99.5% with credits, but request language limiting total annual credits to a percentage of committed spend (standard for us).

Commercial concession ask: to accommodate the renewal protection language, deal desk recommends an additional 3% one-time introductory discount on committed spend (applied to year 1 invoice schedule) in exchange for the guard language above. This is within Marissa's discretionary levers, but flagging for exec signoff due to deviation from standard uplift mechanics.

Attachments: proposed_term_changes_redline.pdf (internal)

Jordan

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 08 Dec 2026 10:22:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: RE: Commercial summary and next steps (QED-2026-042) — exec signoff request

Marissa —

Forwarding the thread. QuantumEdge is strategic (rapid growth customer in adtech) and will commit to a 24-month reserved pool. Procurement is pushing for stronger renewal protection than our default. Jordan from Deal Desk has proposed a compromise that preserves our economics but adds a one-time customer-friendly bridge at renewal and a 5% uplift guard.

Request: executive authorization to grant the 3% one-time introductory concession (applied year 1) and to accept the renewal-protection clause as written if you approve. We believe the concession will close faster and protect long-run ARR.

If you prefer, we can escalate to the CFO for a larger concession, but we’d like to keep this within Revenue scope.

Summary bullets for approval:
- 24-month price lock on committed unit rate
- 5% annual uplift cap during commitment
- Renewal protection: review + 12-month bridge option if renewal uplift >10%
- One-time 3% introductory discount on year 1 committed invoice schedule in exchange for the guard

Please reply with APPROVE / NEEDS CFO / DENY and any language edits.

Grace O'Connor
Director, Deal Desk — Redwood Inference
grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
(408) 555-0142

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 09:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: RE: Commercial summary and next steps (QED-2026-042) — exec signoff request

Grace —

APPROVE with minor edits. I authorize the 3% one-time introductory concession (apply to year 1 committed spend schedule) and accept the renewal-protection framework, provided we:

1) Add a usage threshold clause (minimum committed utilization of 65% over the 24-month term) — if utilization falls below this, the uplift guard is void and we re-price to committed+20% CPI adjustment.
2) Cap cumulative SLA credits at 6% of the annual committed spend (customer-friendly but within risk tolerance).
3) Legal to review final redline to ensure the bridge option is not automatic — it should be contingent on both parties agreeing to an operational plan at renewal.

With those edits, proceed to get QuantumEdge to sign the term sheet and route for DocuSign. Thank you — this seems like a strong strategic win.

Marissa Cole
VP, Revenue Operations — Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
(415) 555-0120

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>

Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 15:43:00 -0800
Subject: Final commercial posture and next steps — QuantumEdge (QED-2026-042)

Lena / Tom —

Thanks for your patience while we worked this internally. Redwood is prepared to proceed on the following mutually agreed commercial posture:

- 24-month commitment with price lock on the committed unit rate
- 5% annual uplift cap applied to list adjustments during the commitment period
- Renewal protection: at first renewal window, any proposed uplift >10% triggers a mutual commercial review; Redwood will offer a one-time 12-month bridge at prior year rates if both parties agree to an operational remediation plan
- One-time 3% introductory discount applied to year 1 committed invoices (as a gesture to expedite execution)
- Usage threshold: uplift guard is contingent on minimum utilization of 65% of committed capacity over the 24 months; below that, standard re-pricing applies
- SLA: 99.5% uptime, with credits capped at 6% of annual committed spend

Attached: QuantumEdge_Term_Summary_v5.pdf, QED_SOW_v2.docx, QED_TermSheet_v3.xlsx
Next steps: legal will publish a clean redline incorporating the usage threshold and the conditional bridge language; once agreed, we will route the TermSheet via DocuSign. HubSpot deal has been updated: https://hubspot.redwood.com/deal/QED-2026-042

If this aligns, please confirm and we will issue the DocuSign packet by EOD tomorrow.

Regards,
Grace O'Connor
Director, Deal Desk — Redwood Inference
